result:
I found 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them. I didn't eyeball each rule: I wrote a script that reads each rule's docstring and compares the function's result with the expected amount over a wide range of qty/unit values. Before the fixes, those 10 rules failed. After the fixes, every rule passes, and every rule raises an error on negative input as expected.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02 | Used `round()`, which can round up, not floor | Floored the discount with `//` |
| 14 | Started at 101 units, not 100 | Changed to `>= 100` |
| 58 | Capped the base price, not the discount | Cap now applies to the discount |
| 72 | Started at 51 units, not 50 | Changed to `>= 50` |
| 79 | Took 4% off instead of 3% | Changed to 3% |
| 84 | Capped the base price, not the discount | Cap now applies to the discount |
| 102 | Started at 6 units, not 5 | Changed to `>= 5` |
| 109 | Started at 6 units, not 5 | Changed to `>= 5` |
| 116 | Capped the base price, not the discount | Cap now applies to the discount |
| 128 | A "marginal" rule that discounted the whole amount | Discount now applies only to units above the threshold: `(qty - 10) * unit` |

STATUS: DONE
